rationale: Domestic drugstore chain; weak F1 fit.

desc: Chinese maker of over-the-counter medicines such as Sanjiu Weitai and Ganmao Ling, along with prescription drugs and health products.
markets: Sold mainly in China, with some exports. Owned by China Resources. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic medicines brand with advertising limits.

desc: Alibaba's health arm operating online pharmacies and healthcare services for Chinese consumers on Tmall and Alibaba platforms.
markets: Operates in mainland China. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic health platform; Alibaba group has global marketing, but this unit is China-focused.

desc: Swiss health and pharmacy group operating Amavita and Sun Store pharmacies and supplying consumer health brands.
markets: Operates in Switzerland. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Swiss domestic pharmacy group; limited global use.

desc: Largest Brazilian pharmacy chain, operating Raia and Drogasil stores and e-commerce selling medicines and beauty products.
markets: Stores across Brazil. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Brazilian domestic pharmacy; limited global use despite Sao Paulo GP.

desc: Chinese traditional medicine maker with Tong Ren Tang brand, selling herbal remedies and operating pharmacies, with stores abroad.
markets: Sells in China and in overseas Chinese communities, with pharmacies in Hong Kong, Europe, Southeast Asia. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Heritage brand might use Chinese GP exposure, though medicine advertising is restricted.

desc: Japanese maker of eye drops, lip balms and skincare, selling Rohto, Mentholatum, Hada Labo and Obagi brands.
markets: Sells in Japan, Asia, the US and Europe. Mentholatum and Obagi operate internationally.
rationale: Skincare and eye care brands could use Asian races and Japanese GP to build recognition.

desc: Japanese drugstore and pharmacy chain operating Sugi Pharmacy stores selling medicines, cosmetics and groceries.
markets: Stores in Japan. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic pharmacy chain; weak F1 fit.

desc: Japanese maker of consumer health and household products such as Netsukaku, Sawaday and Bluelet, sold in Japan and abroad.
markets: Sells in Japan, China, US and Asia. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Japanese consumer-health brand could use Japanese GP; limited global name.

desc: Saudi Arabia's largest pharmacy chain, running Nahdi stores and online sales of medicines, beauty and health products.
markets: Stores across Saudi Arabia. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Saudi domestic pharmacy; Saudi GP could provide local visibility, but pharmacy use is limited.

desc: Japanese discount drugstore chain selling medicines, groceries and household goods through large stores, mainly in Kyushu.
markets: Stores across Japan. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic discount chain with no international exposure.

desc: Japanese drugstore group operating Kusuri no Aoki stores selling medicines, groceries and cosmetics in central Japan.
markets: Stores across Japan. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic drugstore group with no international exposure.

desc: South African pharmacy and health and beauty retailer running Clicks and UPD pharmaceutical distribution businesses.
markets: Stores in South Africa, plus Namibia, Botswana and other African markets. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: South African retailer; F1 has no African race.

desc: Japanese drugstore chain operating Sundrug stores selling medicines, cosmetics, food and daily goods in Japan.
markets: Stores across Japan. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic chain with no international focus.
